Star Trek. Oddly enough, people are shocked that I can effectively love Star Trek, Star Wars, Lord of The Rings and all at the same time. For me it was never a war of one vs. another, it was simply that my own mom turned my attention toward the stars and I made sure it stayed there to a degree.

I’ve sat and watched The Original Series, Deep Space Nine, The Next Generation, Enterprise and Voyager and have found something to love with all of them. I’ve even seen the movies. Consider how many hours of viewing that is and think about that for a second because you’ll need it for perspective. If you need a solid time frame, it’s 546 hours of viewing or 23 days straight. That means, my fellow Trekkies, you and I have probably watched our screens for a combined total of 23 days.

I say that because this one is probably going to be a bit on the long side so, get yourself a cup of whatever, grab a snack, make sure the kids are tucked in and get ready because I’m going to show my fellow Trekkies here somethings they probably haven’t considered while telling you what you already know. I’m not going to sit here and cite sources because this isn’t some scholarly work, it’s just a piece written by me. If any of that is a problem, you can hop off now, no harm no foul but if you find yourself triggered later, fuck you, you were warned.

So The O.G. Series Star Trek was a show set in a time in our future history where space travel and exploration, general cartography of space was of paramount importance. To settle a lot of issues, the socio-political structure was this society that was essentially a utopia where we didn’t have money, everything could be replicated and yeah it was pretty much fantasy but anyway, that’s where it was set. Remember that because it will come up later. Gene Roddenberry’s creation was supposed to be like Wagon Train in Space which it did pretty successfully, treating space as a sort of frontier where, instead of spreading ourselves out, colonizing and wiping out all the indigenous tribes, we’d learn about them and send all that data back to Starfleet to send back to the United Federation of Planets. The phasers were used for defensive measures, Tricorders could do a number of tasks and hyposprays were the instant Get Well Soon cards. We came to care about James Kirk even though he was an egotistical type to some degree, Spock came across as the level-headed guy due to his Vulcan Logic, McCoy hated anything and everything about space travel and transporters…he was our one grumpy fucking uncle, Uhuru was not just eye-candy, she performed a vital role in ship’s comms, Mr. Scott was like Dominic Toretto with a warp core and a Scottish accent, Sulu once went nuts and tried to fence with people and Chekov couldn’t pronounce the word Victor without it becoming “Weektor” or ended up looking for “nuuclear wessels” by asking police about this in San Francisco during the Cold War. Nice going.

Still, with all their character flaws, they were three dimensional and we loved them.

They got cancelled a few times before Trekkies brought them back. They even had an animated series that I watched like crazy as a kid.

There was a film that bored us but we won’t get into that what we will say is the feature-length film versions of Kirk even show how much of a disadvantage time travel could be without prerequisite cash on hand.

Things turned out pretty well for our crew of the Enterprise.

Then we got a look farther into our future with Star Trek: The Next Generation. Now we had an entirely new crew with an entirely new but familiar means of doing what the previous series had done. Spandex was pretty cringeworthy but they dropped that after a bit. We got a look at a new crew with new idiosyncracies and different methods of handling things. That one lasted nine seasons. Pretty impressive. We also got a host of new moral questions with Q constantly fucking about and, spoiler alert…the entire nine seasons were shown to be Q fucking about the entire time. We didn’t get that much more of a look into how Starfleet or The Federation operated until…

Star Trek: Deep Space Nine.

So we now have Benjamin Sisko, commander of a Bajoran Space Station keeping the peace between Cardassians and Bajorans and really boldly going nowhere…at all… We do get a more detailed view of how The Federation works and finally, money is introduced in the form of Gold Pressed Latinum which is basically Latinum, a liquid precious metal poured and stored directly in hollow gold bars. We got The Dominion War and then…The Maquis. Which led us to…

Star Trek: Voyager.

A new crew, an entirely different ship and the absolute best part, the part that had the most potential, they were so far-flung out in space that the Maquis that Janeway and crew had been pursuing, had to pool resources, time and ability with the rest of the Voyager crew. Lost In Space Meets Star Trek. Great concept. Kinda fell short in areas but good.

The Wild Card: The Maquis.
